tasks.short: Build the weekly and monthly people reports for managers and the OR

today.trigger: Monday site meetings, payroll month-close, or a request from the HR Director, an HR business partner or the works council for a cut of headcount, hiring or verzuim.
steps: Export employees, contracts, absence and new hires from AFAS Profit, then add Recruitee hires and Studytube completions where the pack needs them.
Reconcile the export to the previous period and to the latest payroll corrections.
Refresh the Power BI pages or rebuild the Excel pack by site (Rotterdam, Tilburg, Venlo).
Write a short commentary for the HR Director, the site leads and, when it is their cycle, the works council.
File the pack on SharePoint and send it through Outlook.
Answer the first round of questions about what moved.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same headcount, hire and verzuim pivots every week
Retyping the commentary for the company, each site and the works council
Finding which extract is current after payroll corrections
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes on reconciliation after payroll corrections and on cutting the same figures three ways.

lenses.faster: The export, the pivot and the standard pages disappear into the nightly AFAS refresh. What stays is the exception list and the commentary, about an hour a week plus a longer pass in payroll-close week.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS extract starts the refresh, and the standard pages update when every check passes. The analyst is the gate for a failed check, any cut that is not on the list, the commentary, and every pack for the works council.
lenses.ambitious: The HR Director can reallocate the two recruiters across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo every Monday on 90-day retention, a decision that today waits for a quarterly pack. Demand for that weekly decision would grow if it were cheap, especially from the start of peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss copying AFAS exports into Excel and retyping the commentary for every audience. The analyst would want more time on why 90-day retention differs between teams and sites.
lenses.options: A pack that counts only Noordhaven contracts, and a second pack that shows flex hours beside it, lead to different decisions: hire direct, or place a larger order with an agency. A provisional pack marked payroll-not-closed leads the site lead to wait, where a clean pack leads them to move people this week.
lenses.altitude: The week starts with an exception list and a commentary edit, and the analyst gains the right to hold a figure that failed a check. The job is more expert on measurement and lighter on assembly.
reach: The FP&A analyst's monthly headcount-to-budget bridge, once this person learns the AFAS general-ledger cost centres and the finance close calendar.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can tell a real starter from a late payroll correction, and can tell an employee cohort from flex workers who must stay on a separate line. They also judge what a small team allows the works council to see.
tasks.pattern_why: The standard pack is fixed definitions, fixed pages and a fixed calendar on the AFAS extract. Scheduled refresh produces it, and the analyst writes the commentary from figures that have already passed the checks.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract lands, and the Monday job or the payroll-close flag starts the pack.
steps: Refresh the Power BI semantic model from the AFAS extract.
Run the checks: headcount against the prior day, absence rows with no end date, Recruitee hires with no AFAS employee, groups under the agreed minimum size.
Update the standard pages for headcount, time to hire, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding, 90-day retention, and verzuim rate and duration.
Alert the analyst with failed checks and the movements since the previous pack.
The analyst writes the commentary and releases any pack that failed a check or that goes to the works council.
File the pack, the check results and the commentary on SharePoint.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst releases any pack that failed a check, any cut that is not on the standard list, and every pack that goes to the works council.
data_needed: Agreed measure definitions, with flex workers kept on a separate line
Cost centre to site and shift map
Agreed minimum group size
Payroll-close calendar and the works-council reporting calendar
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint list of pack version, checks, commentary author and whether the analyst released it, plus Power BI refresh history.

evidence.claim: Scheduled refresh of a prepared Power BI model is ordinary product behaviour and can produce a standard pack without a model call.
Power BI Copilot can summarise a report and write DAX on Fabric F2 or Premium capacity. Without a prepared model it can misinterpret the data, and non-English chat is not officially supported.
Sick-leave data are health data under GDPR Article 9.
The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens fined a company EUR 15,000 partly because it recorded the cause of sick leave.

risks: A pack built on per-person rows can still be a works-council matter when managers only see totals.
Commentary that guesses a cause for a verzuim spike would process health data.
Flex workers sit in agency portals, so an AFAS-only pack understates the people actually on the floor.
Dutch labels and CAO grade names are a weak spot if a commentary draft is left to Copilot.
research_questions: What share of these 161 hours is a repeated pack with a stable definition, and what share is a one-off cut?
How often does the nightly AFAS extract still disagree with payroll after corrections?
Has the works council already consented to the dataset behind the current dashboards?
Is the flex exclusion written down, and how large is agency headcount relative to the AFAS employee count in peak season?

tasks.short: Get the right people numbers to each site lead on time

today.trigger: A pack is ready, a refresh fails before a site meeting, or a manager writes that they never received last week's figures.
steps: Check that the nightly refresh finished before the Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo meetings.
Keep a private list of who receives the company pack, the site pack and the works-council pack.
Apply site filters so one site does not receive another site's person rows.
Send the file through Outlook and post it on the HR SharePoint site.
Re-send when payroll posts a correction.
Reset access when someone changes site or role.
drudgery: Maintaining the distribution list by hand
Re-sending after a late payroll correction
Answering messages from people who cannot see their own site
today.time_sinks: Failed refreshes are usually found when a manager complains, and the audience list is rebuilt after every reorganisation.

lenses.faster: Subscriptions, row-level security and a refresh-failure alert remove the weekly send and the chase. What stays is a change of audience or a recall, about an hour when the organisation chart changes, plus the failed-refresh cases.
lenses.autonomous: A successful refresh starts delivery to the registered audiences at the agreed time. The analyst is the gate when the refresh fails, when a new audience is requested, and when a correction must replace a pack people have already used.
lenses.ambitious: Night-shift supervisors at Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo would receive their site figures before the shift starts, a group that today hears the numbers later from a day-shift HR business partner. Demand would grow if that delivery were cheap, because the night shifts are a large share of the 750 warehouse and transport staff.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing unread attachments and re-sending the same file. The analyst would want more of the conversation about which figure a site lead will actually use in the shift briefing.
lenses.options: Sending a provisional pack with a visible payroll-not-closed flag leads site leads to hold staffing moves. Holding the pack until the correction lands leads them to decide a day later on figures finance will stand behind.
lenses.altitude: The week becomes audiences, timing and failed sends, and the analyst gains the right to stop or recall a distribution. The job is more expert on access and timing.
reach: The HR administrator's recurring headcount sends, once audience rules are tied to AFAS organisation units and the works council has agreed who may see which site.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst decides whether a new recipient is legitimate when AFAS still shows the old department, and whether a small team would be identifiable if the pack went out.
tasks.pattern_why: Who receives which pack, on which trigger, with which site filter, can be written as subscriptions, row-level security and alerts. Delivery itself does not need a model call.

in_practice.trigger: The semantic-model refresh succeeds, a payroll-correction flag is set, or the clock reaches the agreed send time before a site or shift meeting.
steps: Read refresh status and the reconciliation flags from the reporting pack.
Deliver the registered subscriptions through Power BI, Outlook or Teams, filtered by site.
Suppress any group under the agreed minimum size.
On a payroll correction, replace the prior pack and mark the earlier file withdrawn.
Alert the analyst on a failed refresh, an empty audience or a suppressed small cell.
Write recipient, time, report version and check result to the delivery log.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves a new audience, a recall of a pack people have already used, and any send to the works council or to a staffing agency.
data_needed: Audience register mapped to AFAS organisation units
Row-level security roles by site
Agreed minimum group size
Meeting times per site, including night-shift start
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint delivery log with recipient, report version, timestamp, checks and any recall.

evidence.claim: Power BI subscriptions, data alerts and row-level security can deliver a registered pack on a refresh without a model call.
Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers staffing and hiring information, and warns that faster access to information does not by itself lead to better decisions.
Works-council consent covers arrangements for personal data and facilities able to observe presence, behaviour or performance. The test is what the facility can do.
A consultant reading of Dutch practice holds that totals from a tool which stores per-person rows can still require works-council consent.

risks: A missed site filter sends one site's person-level absence to another site.
A shared night-shift mailbox can turn a staffing pack into de facto monitoring of a small team.
Managers can treat a faster number as a decision while the definition is still wrong.
Audience rules that track who opened a pack would themselves be behaviour monitoring and a works-council matter.
research_questions: How many audiences exist today, and how often does the list change after a reorganisation?
At what time do night-shift supervisors actually need figures, and do they have a company Teams or mail account?
How often is a pack recalled because payroll corrects AFAS after the send?
Has the works council consented to subscriptions on the current dataset, given that the tool stores per-person rows?

tasks.short: Keep the people dashboards, model and measures correct

today.trigger: A CAO grade change, a site or cost-centre split, a new Recruitee stage, a broken visual, or a measure that drifted after an AFAS update.
steps: Find which report, measure or table broke, or which new field is required.
Change the Power BI model, the DAX or the Excel workbook.
Check row counts and totals against AFAS for each site.
Update the definition note on SharePoint so it matches the report.
Republish the app and tell the HR business partners what changed.
Patch the match between agency codes and AFAS cost centres when flex hours land in the wrong place.
drudgery: Hunting a broken measure after an AFAS column rename
Rewriting the same definition in the report and again on SharePoint
Manual row-count checks after every model edit
today.time_sinks: Tracing one wrong verzuim percentage through the extract, the date logic and the flex-worker exclusion.

lenses.faster: Copilot can draft DAX and a first definition note, so the writing of a measure shrinks to a reviewed edit. Testing against AFAS, row-level security and the definition log stays, and that test is still most of the task.
lenses.autonomous: A failed refresh or a schema change opens the work and a draft is prepared in a development workspace. The analyst remains the person who changes a shared measure, because a draft does not publish itself.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the two FP&A analysts: one certified headcount and FTE series, with flex hours on a separate line, that they can take into the forecast at each close. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because finance would use it every month and at each site.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss hunting renamed columns and duplicating definition text. The analyst would want more of the definition work: who counts as a hire, and when a flex worker who takes a Noordhaven contract enters the 90-day cohort.
lenses.options: A measure that excludes flex, and a measure that shows agency hours beside employee headcount, lead finance and HR to different conclusions about whether a site has a vacancy gap or a coding difference. That choice changes the forecast and the hiring plan.
lenses.altitude: More of the week is spent testing and publishing measures, and the analyst gains the right to refuse a measure that has no test against AFAS. The job is more expert.
reach: The controller's monthly tie-out of HR headcount to the ledger, once this person learns the AFAS wage journals and the flex-invoice accrual.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst chooses the definition that matches the CAO and the 90-day North Star, and keeps sickness cause and identifiable small teams out of the model.
tasks.pattern_why: Each update is a design choice about grain, filters and tests. A model can draft DAX and the note, and the analyst remains the author of what is published.

in_practice.trigger: A schema check fails, an HR business partner asks for a new cut, or a CAO or organisation change is logged.
steps: Compare the AFAS extract to the current model and list new, missing and renamed fields.
In a development workspace, draft the DAX and the definition text with Copilot, pointed at the existing measure dictionary.
Test totals against AFAS for each site, for employees and flex separately, on a known payroll period.
The analyst edits the definition, the minimum group size and the row-level security role.
Publish to the shared app and append the change to the definition log.
Tell the HR business partners and FP&A what moved.
in_practice.human_gate: No measure, page or definition reaches the shared workspace unless the analyst publishes it.
data_needed: Current semantic model and measure dictionary
AFAS field list for employee, contract, absence and cost centre
CAO grade map
Written rule for how flex workers and agency hours are treated
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint definition log with measure name, version, test result, publisher and date.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot writes DAX and summarises reports on a prepared model, on Fabric F2 or Premium. It can misinterpret data without that model, and non-English chat is not officially supported.
Uber's QueryGPT cut writing a query from about 10 minutes to about 3, and 78 percent of early users said it saved time. Hallucinated table and column names remained unsolved.
Typical defects in an AFAS people extract are a missing contract end date and a sickness case left open. Rules can detect them. HR administration corrects the source record.

risks: A drafted measure that counts sickness cause, or that shows a group small enough to identify someone, can look finished and still be unfit to publish.
Dutch field names sit outside Copilot's official language support, so column matches will be wrong unless the dictionary is prepared.
HR and finance can publish two headcount truths if the flex rule is only in someone's head.
There is no documented Dutch customer result for this use.
research_questions: Is the semantic model documented well enough that a drafted measure stops inventing columns?
How many broken measures in the last two quarters came from an AFAS rename, and how many from a real definition change?
Do HR and finance already differ on headcount by enough to move the forecast?
Does the current Power BI capacity include Fabric F2 or Premium, which Copilot requires?

tasks.short: Answer managers when a people number looks wrong or missing

today.trigger: A Teams or Outlook message from an HR business partner, a site lead or the HR Director about a figure, a filter or an access error.
steps: Read the question and open the same report under that person's site.
Check filters, row-level security and whether they are in the right app.
Compare the figure with AFAS for the period they named.
Explain the definition in plain language, in Dutch.
Fix a broken slicer or send a corrected export when the report is wrong.
Note the question if it has come up before.
drudgery: Repeating the definition of verzuim rate and time to hire
Walking people through the same filters with screenshots
Resetting access after a site transfer
today.time_sinks: Questions that arrive without the page, the site and the period, so the context is rebuilt from scratch.

lenses.faster: A read-only draft from verified measures removes the repeated definition and filter replies. What stays is approval of any reply that states a figure, plus the questions that match no verified measure, which are the longer ones.
lenses.autonomous: A message in the people-data Teams channel starts a draft answer from the prepared model. The analyst approves every reply that states a figure before it is sent, and writes the reply when the verified list has no match.
lenses.ambitious: Warehouse team leads, day and night, would get answers on team-level rates directly, a group that today has to wait for one of three HR business partners. Demand would grow if that were cheap, because there are many more team leads than HR business partners.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss the repeated tour of the same slicers. The analyst would want more of the disputes that show a definition is wrong.
lenses.options: An answer with employees only, and an answer with agency hours beside it, lead a planner to different decisions: recruit, or place a flex order. The analyst chooses which answer is released.
lenses.altitude: Repeated explanations leave the week, and the remaining questions are the ones the verified list cannot answer. The analyst gains the right to let a verified, approved answer stand. The job is more expert.
reach: The HR business partner's routine weekly verzuim question for a site, once the analyst learns that site's shift pattern and the boundary of what the business partner still discusses with the manager.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst hears when a question about a number is really about one employee, a conflict or a possible dismissal, and stops the assistant there. They also catch a confident answer that would be repeated in a site meeting while it is still wrong.
tasks.pattern_why: The questions are not known in advance, so a fixed pack cannot cover them. The assistant may read only a prepared model, it must say it is AI, and the analyst approves any figure before it counts.

in_practice.trigger: A Teams message in the people-data channel, or a comment on a Power BI report.
steps: Resolve the person to a site role and reject questions about an individual employee, a sickness cause or a performance judgement.
Draft an answer only from the verified measure list, with the definition, the filter and the period, and with a line that the reply comes from an AI assistant.
Suppress the draft when the group is under the agreed minimum size.
Send the draft to the analyst.
On approval, post it in the same thread.
If no verified measure fits, leave the thread with the analyst, who answers or corrects the model.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst approves every reply that states a figure before it is sent, and writes any reply the verified measure list cannot support.
data_needed: Verified measure list with Dutch definitions
Row-level security by site
Agreed minimum group size
The asker's site role
in_practice.logs_to: The Teams thread and a SharePoint log of question, measure used, whether the analyst approved it, and whether the model was later corrected.

evidence.claim: Visier Vee answers people-analytics questions in Teams or Slack. Its tenfold claim is the vendor's, with no customer named.
Microsoft's Workforce Insights agent shows managers staffing and hiring information, and warns that faster access does not by itself lead to better decisions.
Power BI Copilot answers questions on a prepared semantic model and can misinterpret the data without one. Non-English chat is not officially supported.
People must be told when they are interacting with an AI system.
In a Visier survey, 48 percent of 1,000 US employees said they had exaggerated their use of AI.

risks: A wrong figure, approved in a hurry, will be repeated in a site meeting and may reach the works council.
Dutch questions sit outside Copilot's official language support, so an unprepared model will misread CAO and verzuim terms.
Team-lead access to verzuim can slide into lookups of one person's absence, which is health data.
A question-answering facility on per-person rows needs works-council consent before it is switched on. Productivity-style views usually qualify, and a missing consent can be voided within a month.
research_questions: In a typical month, how many manager questions map onto a measure that already exists, and how many are definition disputes or individual cases?
Will the works council consent to a conversational layer on this dataset before it is turned on?
Are the questions in Dutch, and who will maintain the Dutch definitions the assistant is allowed to quote?
Can success be read from the ticket and rework log, given that self-reported AI use runs high?

tasks.short: Find sites, shifts and agencies the people reports do not cover

today.trigger: The HR Director asks which site, shift or agency needs attention, or the analyst reviews open roles, flex orders and certificate cover before a planning meeting.
steps: Ask the three HR business partners which managers are raising a gap.
List open Recruitee roles by site and shift and see which have a thin pipeline.
Compare flex-agency orders and hours, from the three agency portals, with the vacancy plan.
Check Studytube for forklift, VCA and food-safety certificates that expire before the work is planned.
Note sites and shifts that never appear in HR's questions.
Write a short note for the HR Director.
drudgery: Collecting flex orders from three separate agency portals
Copying certificate expiry lists out of Studytube
Rebuilding the same site comparison in Excel
today.time_sinks: Agency hours and AFAS headcount do not share a key, so the comparison is redone by hand each time.

lenses.faster: The weekly gap list, built from Recruitee, Studytube and the agency exports, replaces the chase around HR business partners. What stays is about three quarters of an hour to judge which flags are real and to decide what is put in front of the HR Director.
lenses.autonomous: A Monday job, or a rise in agency orders above the seasonal band, starts the gap list. The analyst is the gate for putting a site, shift or agency on the HR Director's agenda.
lenses.ambitious: A new fortnightly flex-readiness note for the Venlo warehouse manager: open roles, agency hours on order, and forklift and VCA cover before peak. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because the same note would then be worth running every two weeks at Tilburg and Rotterdam as their peaks start.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss chasing three agency portals and pasting the totals into Excel. The analyst would want more time on whether a gap is a recruiting problem or a certificate problem.
lenses.options: A flag of no candidates, and a flag of candidates stuck at offer, lead to different decisions: spend more on attraction, or change the offer within the CAO. A certificate shortfall leads to a Studytube enrolment push before any extra hiring.
lenses.altitude: A weekly gap list replaces asking around, and the analyst gains the right to place a site or an agency on the HR Director's agenda because a threshold fired. The job is more expert on what those thresholds mean.
reach: The recruiter's weekly tally of stuck requisitions in Recruitee, once this person learns the stage definitions and which delays the recruiter is able to fix.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst can tell a recruiting gap from an expired certificate or a portal that was not updated, and the conversation with the three staffing agencies stays with a person.
tasks.pattern_why: The gaps are joins and thresholds across Recruitee, Studytube, AFAS and the agency exports. Those rules can be written down and run on a schedule.

in_practice.trigger: Monday 06:00, or an agency-hours export that sits above the agreed seasonal band for a site.
steps: Load the latest Recruitee pipeline, Studytube certificate expiries, AFAS open roles and the agency order export.
Flag a site or shift with open roles and a thin pipeline, certificates expiring before the planned work, or agency hours far from the vacancy plan.
Keep flex hours on a separate line from employee headcount.
Suppress any flag that would identify a person, including a team under the minimum size.
Post the gap list to the analyst.
The analyst chooses which items go to the HR Director, the recruiters or the Venlo warehouse manager.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst decides which flags are acted on, and any contact with a staffing agency stays with the analyst or the recruiter.
data_needed: Recruitee stage definitions and open requisitions by site and shift
Studytube certificate type, expiry, site and whether the certificate is mandatory on that shift
Agency order and hours exports with a cost-centre code
Seasonal bands for flex hours by site
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint log of each flag, the source files, the threshold, and the analyst's decision to escalate or close it.

evidence.claim: Coverage rules on open requisitions, certificate expiry and agency hours can be scheduled checks. Whether the three agency portals can supply a file, rather than a screen, is unproven here.

Works-council consent is required for a facility that can observe behaviour or performance. Monitoring who opened a report would fall under that test. A coverage list of roles, hours and certificates is a different facility and still needs a consent check.
No opened source in the digest reports a Dutch result or a works-council decision on this kind of monitor.

risks: Tracking who opened a dashboard would be behaviour monitoring and a works-council matter, so the monitor has to stay on workforce gaps.
Flex hours that cannot be tied to an AFAS cost centre will produce false gaps.
Certificate flags can identify one employee on a small shift if the minimum group size is ignored.
Commercial customer analysis is a different job. If that is what the business wants, it belongs with FP&A.
research_questions: Can the three staffing agencies provide orders, hours and invoices as files with a cost-centre code, or are the portals screen-only?
Does Studytube already store forklift, VCA and food-safety expiry in a way that can be joined to a shift?
Would a gap list change a recruiting or planning decision within two weeks, or would it sit unread?
Is any part of this task actually about Noordhaven's shipping customers, which would move it out of HR?

tasks.short: Design a new people report or model when the current one falls short

today.trigger: The HR Director or an HR business partner asks a question the current app cannot answer, or a workbook has spread so far that the figures no longer match.
steps: Write down the question, the grain and who will see the result.
Sketch the fields from AFAS, Recruitee or Studytube and the Excel the requester already keeps.
Build a dataset, a Power BI page or a new workbook.
Set site filters and test totals against AFAS.
Walk one HR business partner through the draft and adjust it.
Publish the app or send the workbook, and file a short definition note.
drudgery: Starting from a blank workbook for a question that is close to one already published
Rebuilding slicers and access for each new page
Writing the data dictionary after the fact
today.time_sinks: The long part is agreeing the grain and then discovering that the AFAS extract does not hold the field the requester assumed.

lenses.faster: A first draft of the model, the DAX and the specification takes minutes in a development workspace. The analyst still spends the larger share on the grain, the AVG and works-council boundary, and the acceptance test with the requester.
lenses.autonomous: A written request starts a draft in a workspace that nobody else uses. The draft stays there until the analyst accepts the tests and publishes.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the two recruiters: each accepted offer shown through week-one onboarding and still-here at day 90, by site and by source, direct hire or named agency. Demand would grow if it were cheap, because both recruiters would use it through the year and the HR Director would use it when agency contracts are renewed.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss rebuilding slicers and filling the same dictionary rows. The analyst would want more of the design of the 90-day cohort and the argument about what productive means at Noordhaven.
lenses.options: A person-level tool and a team-level tool lead to different decisions about whether it can be switched on. The team-level tool can go ahead under the cell-size rule. The person-level tool waits for works-council consent and still excludes sickness cause and appraisal scores.
lenses.altitude: Fewer hours go into blank workbooks, and more go into the acceptance test with the requester. The analyst gains the right to set the grain and to refuse a design that stores health or performance detail. The job is more expert.
reach: The learning and development specialist's certificate workbook for forklift, VCA and food safety, once this person learns which certificates are mandatory on which shifts and how Studytube stores expiry.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst sets the grain and the consent boundary before the tool exists, and refuses a design that would show sickness cause, an individual score or a team small enough to identify someone.
tasks.pattern_why: A model can draft the specification, the DAX and a first page. Whether the tool may exist, at which grain, and with which fields, remains the analyst's decision.

in_practice.trigger: A written request from the HR Director, an HR business partner, a recruiter or FP&A for a question the current app cannot answer.
steps: Record the decision the new view must support, the grain, the audience and the fields it is allowed to hold.
Check whether the facility needs works-council consent before build, and stop there until that consent exists.
Draft the model, DAX and page with Copilot in a development workspace, from the measure dictionary.
Test totals against AFAS, and test that sickness cause and individual appraisal scores cannot be reached.
Run an acceptance test with the requester on a known payroll period.
The analyst publishes to the shared app with row-level security, or sends the requester back to a change of grain.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst publishes, and a design that can show individual performance or individual absence waits for works-council consent and a named overseer.
data_needed: The decision the view must support
Measure dictionary and allowed field list
AFAS, Recruitee and Studytube field availability
Works-council consent status for any new facility
Agreed minimum group size
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint definition log: request, grain, consent status, test result, publisher and date.

evidence.claim: Power BI Copilot writes DAX and report drafts on a prepared model, and can misinterpret data without one. Non-English chat is not officially supported.
Uber's QueryGPT reduced query-writing time from about 10 minutes to about 3, while hallucinated table and column names remained.
Works-council consent is judged by what a facility can observe. Productivity dashboards usually qualify, and a missing consent can be voided within one month.
Commentary on the Digital Omnibus puts the high-risk duties for workplace AI that evaluates performance from 2 December 2027, including a competent overseer and logs.

risks: A workbook emailed to a site lead carries person rows outside row-level security.
A cohort view of individual 90-day outcomes can become a performance tool and then needs consent now and, from 2 December 2027, the high-risk duties.
Drafted DAX on a new model will invent fields, especially where the names are Dutch.
A tool the works council has not agreed can be voided within a month.
research_questions: Which new reports requested in the last year were still used two months after delivery?
Do site leads require Excel, and would that copy sit outside row-level security?
What is the works council's usual lead time for a consent request on a new people-data facility?
Can week-one onboarding be defined from Studytube completions and AFAS start dates alone?

tasks.short: Compile hire, transfer and absence statistics from the personnel records

today.trigger: Payroll month-close, the works-council cycle, or an HR business partner preparing a site review of hires, transfers and verzuim.
steps: Pull hires, transfers, contract changes and absence rows from AFAS Profit.
Chase HR administration for missing end dates, open sickness cases and employees with no site.
Compute counts and rates by site and by month, and a separate line for flex where the data exists.
Add review-conversation completion if appraisals are in scope, without the scores.
Paste the tables into the monthly workbook and the works-council annex.
Answer questions about why a site moved.
drudgery: Exporting the same personnel lists after every payroll close
Chasing missing end dates and sickness cases left open
Rebuilding the works-council annex from the workbook
today.time_sinks: Absence lists and hire lists that do not match the previous month because a correction landed after the export.

lenses.faster: The monthly counts and rates are produced by the refresh and the checks, so the rebuild disappears. What stays is the exception list for HR administration and the analyst's certification, about an hour in a normal week and a longer pass when the works-council pack is due.
lenses.autonomous: Payroll close starts the compile. Internal totals update when every check passes and small groups are suppressed. The analyst handles failed checks, and approves the version that goes to the works council.
lenses.ambitious: On the second working day after absence records update, the HR Director and the site leads can decide which teams need a conversation about verzuim or early exits, every week. Demand for that weekly decision would grow if it were cheap, because peak-season cover and the reintegration deadlines do not wait for month-end.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss exporting absence lists and rebuilding the same rates. The analyst would want more time on which shifts lose people before day 90.
lenses.options: A series of employees only, and a series with flex starters shown separately, lead to different decisions about Venlo: a retention problem among Noordhaven contracts, or an agency-volume effect. The hiring plan changes with that choice.
lenses.altitude: The series updates without a rebuild, and the analyst gains the right to certify or hold the monthly figures the works council sees. The job is more expert on the series and less clerical.
reach: The payroll specialist's tie-out of FTE and contract hours to the pay run, once this person learns the AFAS payroll components and paid hours under the transport CAO. The pay calculation stays with payroll.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst explains a movement in hires or verzuim to the HR Director and the works council with the cause of sickness left out. The reintegration file and its statutory deadlines stay with the HR business partner and the company doctor.
tasks.pattern_why: Hires, transfers, review-completion counts and verzuim rates are defined counts and durations on the AFAS extract. Rules can compute them and can flag broken source rows. HR administration corrects the rows.

in_practice.trigger: Payroll close, and the daily extract for the running internal totals.
steps: Run the statistical queries on the AFAS extract for hires, transfers, review-conversation completion, and verzuim rate and duration by site and month.
Flag missing contract end dates, sickness cases left open, employees with no site, and Recruitee hires with no employee number.
Suppress groups under the agreed minimum size, and keep absence cause and appraisal scores out of the output.
Send source-record failures to HR administration for correction in AFAS.
Rebuild only the affected totals after the correction.
The analyst certifies the monthly series and releases the works-council version.
in_practice.human_gate: HR administration corrects source records. The analyst certifies the monthly series and approves the version that goes to the works council. Individual absence cases stay with the HR business partner.
data_needed: AFAS employee, contract, transfer and absence start and end, with cause excluded from the extract
Site and cost-centre map
Review-conversation completion flag, with scores excluded
Agreed minimum group size
Works-council calendar
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint log of each run: checks, rows sent back to HR administration, totals certified, and the works-council release.

evidence.claim: Missing contract end dates and sickness cases left open are detectable with rules on an AFAS extract. Correction of the personnel record sits with HR administration.
Sick-leave data are health data under GDPR Article 9.
The Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens fined a company EUR 15,000 partly because it recorded the cause of sick leave.
A person may not be subject to a solely automated decision that has a legal or similarly significant effect.
Works-council consent applies to personal-data arrangements and to facilities that can observe behaviour or performance.

risks: An extract that still contains absence cause repeats the kind of processing the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens has fined.
Individual flags on who may leave, or who is often absent, would be a significant decision about a worker and need a person.
Appraisal scores in the statistical pack slide into performance evaluation and toward the high-risk duties from 2 December 2027.
Flex workers are missing from AFAS, so employee-only rates misstate the floor during peak.
research_questions: Does the AFAS absence table store cause today, and can that field be kept out of the extract used for reporting?
Who certifies the figure the works council receives today, and will they accept certification by this analyst?
Are appraisal scores stored in AFAS, and can the pack be limited to completion counts?
By which working day after payroll are absence end dates stable enough for a day-2 verzuim rate?

tasks.short: Summarise logistics labour-market trends that affect hiring or pay

today.trigger: The annual pay review, a CAO round, peak-season planning, or the HR Director asking whether a site is getting harder to hire for.
steps: Collect CAO wage tables, public labour-market notes and the agency rate cards the company already holds.
Pull Noordhaven's own time to hire, offer acceptance and 90-day retention by site.
Read the material and mark which figures come from which source.
Draft a note on what the figures mean for drivers and warehouse staff at the three sites.
Discuss the draft with the compensation and benefits specialist.
Join calls with an agency or a sector contact when the note is not enough.
drudgery: Saving wage surveys and CAO PDFs into a folder with no index
Rebuilding the same three-site comparison before every peak
Copying vendor headlines into a note without the limitation underneath
today.time_sinks: Finding a current, citeable Dutch figure for warehouse and driver tightness around Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, then discovering it is national and too broad for one site.

lenses.faster: The first brief, with a source under each figure and a caveat where the source does not support a cause, replaces a morning of collecting. What stays is checking every figure and writing what Noordhaven should do, about half a day a few times a month.
lenses.autonomous: The first Monday of the month, or the opening of a CAO round or a peak-season plan, starts the draft. The draft waits for the analyst. External calls stay with the analyst or the compensation specialist.
lenses.ambitious: Before each peak and each CAO round, the compensation specialist and the HR Director decide whether Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo needs a temporary market allowance, a decision that today is mostly annual and company-wide. Demand would grow if the brief were cheap, because the three local markets would each justify a brief whenever they move.
lenses.joy: Nobody would miss filing PDF wage surveys and rewriting the same site table. The analyst would want more of the argument about what a tight local driver market means for the pay band.
lenses.options: A tight-market reading and a reading that the next CAO increase already covers the gap lead to different decisions: open a temporary allowance at one site, or wait for the collective agreement. Those are different costs.
lenses.altitude: A sourced brief arrives for editing, and the analyst gains the right to attach a caveat the HR Director has to see before a pay proposal. External contacts stay in the role, so the judgement work is more expert.
reach: The compensation and benefits specialist's first comparison of local pay to the CAO scales, once this person learns the Beroepsgoederenvervoer scales, the warehouse CAO, and which allowances the company may still set.

tasks.human_edge: The analyst judges what a national or sector figure means for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo. Calls with agencies, UWV, the unions or the works council stay with a person, as does any pay recommendation.
tasks.pattern_why: Each scan turns an agreed set of sources into one brief with citations and caveats, inside a fixed monthly workflow. The steps of the brief are known in advance. The calls outside the company are not part of the model step.

in_practice.trigger: The first Monday of the month, and the date a CAO round or a peak-season plan is opened.
steps: Load the agreed source list and Noordhaven's own time to hire, offer acceptance and 90-day retention by site.
Draft a short note that places a source under every figure and states when a source does not support a cause.
The analyst checks each figure against the source document.
The analyst writes the implication separately for Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo, including whether a CAO increase already covers the gap.
The compensation specialist receives the note only after that edit.
Any call to an agency, UWV, a union or the works council is made by the analyst or the compensation specialist.
in_practice.human_gate: The analyst signs the note before anyone relies on it, and makes or joins any external contact. The note may not recommend an individual pay decision.
data_needed: Agreed Dutch sources, such as the current CAO texts and the public series compensation already trusts
Noordhaven time to hire, offer acceptance and 90-day retention by site
Agency rate cards the company is allowed to use
The calendar of CAO rounds and peak-season plans
in_practice.logs_to: A SharePoint folder per note with the draft, the sources opened, the analyst's corrections and the signed version.

evidence.claim: Workday's published workforce report does not establish how much of the described workforce change AI caused. A trend note has to keep that kind of caveat.
Visier Vee is sold as a people-analytics assistant, and its tenfold claim names no customer. A brief that repeats a vendor headline needs the underlying source.
No opened page in the digest gives a Dutch labour-market result or a works-council decision. The analyst has to verify every Dutch figure the draft cites.
In a Visier survey, 48 percent of 1,000 US employees had exaggerated their AI use, so felt time saved is a weak test of this brief.

risks: A drafted figure with a broken or national source will be treated as a local wage fact for Venlo or the port.
Vendor headlines about AI and jobs will enter a pay discussion without the caveat that the source does not show a cause.
A trend note that names individuals who might leave would cross into performance and absence scoring.
Dutch-language CAO and UWV pages are exactly where an unattended draft is most likely to misread a number.
research_questions: Which external series has compensation already treated as decisive: CAO texts, UWV, CBS, a sector body, or the agency rate cards?
Has any labour-market note in the past year changed an allowance or a vacancy approval?
Who checks Dutch-language sources, and how long does that check take on a real CAO table?
Would a site-level brief before peak change a decision the annual review does not already make?

role.altitude: The analyst becomes the owner of the metric layer that managers, HR business partners, finance and a read-only assistant query: definitions, who may see a figure, verified answers, and the checks that hold a figure back. 90-day retention and verzuim are ready on the second working day after payroll, and routine questions no longer wait on this person.
reach: The FP&A analyst's workforce-cost bridge from AFAS headcount and FTE into the forecast, after the close calendar and wage accounts are learned.
The controller's monthly tie-out between HR headcount and the ledger, including the flex accrual.
The payroll specialist's FTE and contract-hours reconciliation to the pay run, with the pay calculation left in payroll.
The recruiter's Recruitee stage tally and stuck-requisition list, with candidate assessment and offers left to the recruiter.
The learning and development specialist's counts of valid forklift, VCA and food-safety certificates by site and shift.
The compensation and benefits specialist's first comparison of local pay to the CAO scales, ahead of a market-allowance proposal.
The HR business partner's routine site questions on verzuim and starter cohorts, with the manager conversation and the reintegration file left to the business partner.
The HR administrator's repeated headcount extracts, once audience and correction rules are in the model.
role.ceiling_note: One full-time analyst at this loaded cost cannot also run reintegration cases, payroll, recruiting conversations or agency negotiations. The ceiling is the kind of work as much as the hours: absence cause stays out under AVG, individual scores stay out, flex hours often sit in three agency portals, and a new facility waits on the works council. Three sites and two shift patterns add volume in peak season without adding hours. Power BI Copilot also needs the right capacity, and its Dutch answers need a prepared model. No opened source shows a Dutch peer result.
skills_to_grow: AFAS Profit's employee, contract, absence and payroll tables, and the month-close sequence
Power BI semantic models, DAX, row-level security and refresh monitoring, including the Fabric capacity Copilot requires
AVG Article 9 in practice: health data, agreed minimum group sizes, and the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens line on sickness cause
Works-council consent under WOR article 27, and how to brief the OR before a new people-data facility
The CAO Beroepsgoederenvervoer and the warehouse CAO: grades, hours and allowances the company may still set
EU AI Act duties for workplace systems that evaluate people, including a named overseer and logs, from 2 December 2027
role.ambitious_version: The analyst keeps one certified layer for the North Star, by site and by shift, including night teams and flex workers who later take a Noordhaven contract. By the second working day the HR Director can see 90-day retention, week-one onboarding and verzuim and can move the two recruiters while that cohort is still open. HR business partners, team leads and FP&A take routine answers from the same layer. The analyst spends the remaining time on why one shift keeps people and another does not, and on the consent and definition choices that make those figures safe to show the works council.
